description: Switch Claude Code accounts per window or repository and see every account's plan limits in the status bar. Not affiliated with Anthropic.
cmd.setRepoDefault: Set default account for this repository
cmd.clearRepoDefault: Clear default account for this repository
cmd.toggleHistorySharing: Share / stop sharing history across accounts
cfg.scope: Where the selected account is remembered.
cfg.scope.workspace: Each window/repository remembers its own account (extension storage; nothing is written to the repository).
cfg.scope.user: A single account for every window (each window picks it up when reloaded).
cfg.accountsRoot: Folder where accounts are created. Empty = `~/.claude-accounts`.
cfg.sharedItems: Items from ~/.claude that shared-profile accounts use through links. Credentials and .claude.json always stay per account.
cfg.shareHistory: All accounts use the same conversation history from `~/.claude`. Changing this (here or with the **Share / stop sharing history across accounts** command) opens a dialog that merges existing history when turning on, or lets each account keep a copy or start empty when turning off.
cfg.historyItems: Items treated as history, linked only while `#claudeAccounts.shareHistory#` is on: per-folder conversations (`projects`), prompt history (`history.jsonl`), checkpoints (`file-history`) and `todos`. `plans` is never linked: Claude Code refuses to save plans through a link.
cfg.autoApplyRepoDefault: When a repository is opened, automatically apply the default account set for it.
cfg.reloadBehavior: What to do after switching accounts. The Claude Code extension only reads the environment when it loads, so a reload is needed; it also closes the open Claude Code conversation and terminals in this window. After the reload your last sent prompt is typed back into Claude Code and copied to the clipboard (pasted images are not carried over).
cfg.applyToTerminal: Also set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in this window's integrated terminals so the `claude` CLI uses the same account.
cfg.loginCommand: Command run in the terminal to log in to an account.
cfg.statusBarStyle: How the current account appears in the status bar.
cfg.statusBarStyle.name: Icon and full name, e.g. Claude: Work.
cfg.showPlan: Show the account's plan (e.g. Pro, Max 20x) in the status bar and the account picker, when Claude Code provides it.
cfg.rules: Default-account rules, checked in order when no default is set for the specific repository. A pattern starting with ~, / or a drive letter matches the folder path (e.g. ~/work/**); anything else matches the git remote (e.g. github.com/my-company/*). Without wildcards, a pattern also matches everything below it.
cfg.suggestSwitchOnLimit: When the current account hits its usage limit in this window, offer to switch to another account. Not used while `#claudeAccounts.autoSwitchOnLimit#` switches automatically.
cfg.autoSwitchOnLimit: When the current account hits its usage limit in this window, switch to the account with the most headroom and reload without asking. If no other account has headroom, `#claudeAccounts.suggestSwitchOnLimit#` applies.
cfg.remindOnLimitReset: When the current account hits its usage limit and you stay on it, notify when the limit resets and offer to continue: the interrupted conversation opens with `continue` typed in, and you press Enter.
cfg.experimental.autoContinue: **Experimental, at your own risk (Windows only).** After the reset, send `continue` by itself: once keyboard and mouse have been idle for `#claudeAccounts.experimental.autoContinueIdleSeconds#` seconds, this VS Code window is brought to the front and `continue` + Enter is typed into Claude Code as real keystrokes. Retries every minute for up to 6 hours; several waiting windows take turns. Keystrokes go to whatever is in front, so a window that pops up at that moment could receive them. With `#claudeAccounts.autoSwitchOnLimit#` and shared history, the account switched to continues the same conversation the same way. Needs `#claudeAccounts.remindOnLimitReset#`.
cfg.gravatar: Show the Gravatar of each account's e-mail in the account picker. Off by default: when on, the extension requests images from gravatar.com, sending a hash of the e-mail.
cfg.artifactPreview: Preview artifacts that Claude Code publishes on a local page (http://127.0.0.1), from any account, without logging into claude.ai. Artifacts are found in the local session logs; only those published from local files can be shown.
cfg.artifactPreviewPort: Port of the local artifact preview (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`). Change it if another program already uses it.
cfg.artifactPreviewAutoOpen: Open the local preview in the browser as soon as a new artifact is published. When off, a notification offers to open it. Needs `#claudeAccounts.artifactPreview#`.
cfg.planLimits: Show each account's 5-hour and 7-day plan limits. Read every minute from the same endpoint Claude Code's /usage uses; no tokens are used.
cfg.reloadBehavior.ask: Ask whether to reload now or later.
cfg.reloadBehavior.never: Don't reload; only show a reminder to reload.
cfg.experimental.keepCacheWarm: **Experimental, at your own risk (Windows only).** Keeps the prompt cache of a large conversation (at least `#claudeAccounts.experimental.keepCacheWarmMinContext#` tokens of context) warm while you are away: shortly before the cache expires, and only after keyboard and mouse have been idle for `#claudeAccounts.experimental.keepCacheWarmIdleSeconds#` seconds, this VS Code window is brought to the front and a short ping (`[keep-alive] Reply only with OK and do nothing else.`) is typed into Claude Code. Each ping reads the whole context, which counts toward your plan limits and adds two messages to the conversation, so it stops after `#claudeAccounts.experimental.keepCacheWarmPings#` pings until you send a prompt yourself. Skipped while Claude is still working or a usage limit is reached.
cfg.experimental.keepCacheWarmPings: How many keep-alive pings at most after your last prompt. Each one keeps the cache for one more cache lifetime (5 minutes or 1 hour, as Claude Code uses it).
cfg.experimental.autoContinueIdleSeconds: Seconds without keyboard or mouse input before `#claudeAccounts.experimental.autoContinue#` types `continue`.
cfg.experimental.keepCacheWarmMinContext: Smallest conversation context, in tokens, that `#claudeAccounts.experimental.keepCacheWarm#` keeps warm. Smaller conversations are cheap to rebuild.
cfg.experimental.afterTyping: When a keep-alive ping or auto-continue had to end the screen saver to type, what comes back afterwards: the screen saver, or the screen turned off (no light at all, good for OLED).
cfg.experimental.preventSleep: Windows: keep the computer from sleeping while a keep-alive ping or auto-continue is waiting, so it can still be typed. The screen and screen saver turn off as usual.
cfg.experimental.keepCacheWarmIdleSecond: Seconds without keyboard or mouse input before `#claudeAccounts.experimental.keepCacheWarm#` sends a ping.
